original_value: AbstractThis article contributes to the general program of extending techniques and ideas of effective algebra to computable metric space theory. It is well-known that relative computable categoricity (to be defined) of a computable algebraic structure is equivalent to having a c.e. Scott family with finitely many parameters (e.g., [1]). The first main result of the article extends this characterisation to computable Polish metric spaces. The second main result illustrates that just a slight change of the definitions will give us a new notion of categoricity unseen in the countable case (to be stated formally). The second result also shows that the characterisation of computably categorical closed subspaces of ${\Cal R}^n $ contained in [17] cannot be improved. The third main result extends the characterisation to not necessarily separable structures of cardinality κ using κ-computability.

It is well known that, for a computable algebraic structure, relative computable categoricity (to be defined) is equivalent to having a c.e. Scott family with finitely many parameters (e.g., [1]). The article’s first main result extends this characterization to computable Polish metric spaces. Its second main result shows that a slight modification of the definitions yields a new notion of categoricity not seen in the countable case (to be stated formally), and also demonstrates that the characterization of computably categorical closed subspaces of ${\Cal R}^n$ in [17] cannot be improved. The third main result extends the characterization to nonseparable structures of cardinality κ by means of κ-computability.
